docs: docs/en/browser-support.md and docs/ko/browser-support.md state these targets, and describe what each exception costs a reader

exceptions.reason: The focus ring around a field shell, a Rating star and a selectable DataTable, and the pill or line a server-rendered Tabs bar draws on its chosen tab until the indicator is measured. A field still shows focus through its border or fill and a DataTable through its active row, a Rating falls back to :focus-within under @supports not selector(:has(*)), and the chosen tab is told apart by its colour alone until the page hydrates.

Centres the box or icon beside a label on the label's first line, reserves the height a StreamingText holds before its first word lands, and sets a PromptInput's minimum and maximum rows. Without it the box sits at the top of the line, the reserved height is the line-height the browser computed rather than one line of this text, and the prompt field falls back to its rows attribute.
Tailwind's own registered properties, which carry a fallback of their own. Nothing in the library's own rules registers a property.

Swaps ScrollArea's left and right edge fades in a right-to-left layout, and turns the Skeleton and indeterminate ProgressLinear sweeps around in one. Without it the fades are not swapped, and a sweep runs leftwards only inside an element with dir="rtl" — inside an LTR island in such an element as well.

Makes the surfaces opaque and takes the backdrop blur off for a reader whose system asks for reduced transparency. A browser without the media feature never matches the block, so the reader gets the translucent surfaces over a blurred backdrop that every reader without the setting gets.
Hides the scrollbar of a strip that draws its own controls. The same rule hides it through ::-webkit-scrollbar in the browsers that lack this property.
A multiline TextField's resize handle, and WindowPane's. Safari on iOS and Firefox for Android draw no resize handle at all, so there is nothing to fall back to.
The pointer's shape over a control. Safari on iOS only draws a pointer on an iPad with a pointing device attached, and falls back to the default one for every keyword the data lists as unsupported.
The colour of selected text in a field. Safari on iOS keeps its own selection colour.

`neba/a2ui` reads its own catalog with `import … with { type: 'json' }`, which is the only form Node's ESM resolver accepts for JSON. It is not on the package's barrel and cannot be reached without also installing `@a2ui/react`, so the only way to meet it is a build that bundles an A2UI renderer — and every bundler that can parse the attribute resolves the specifier at build time, which is where it stops. Nothing a reader can see depends on it; what it rules out is loading that one subpath as raw ESM in a browser older than Chrome 123, which is not a way a React renderer is loaded. The rest of the package never imports it.

Draws an Animate* that is waiting for its trigger as it ends when scripting is turned off, since nothing will ever start it, and draws the final text of AnimateTyping, AnimateScramble and AnimateCounter, which only a script would otherwise reach. A browser without the feature skips those rules, and with scripting off there the effect stays on its first frame, which for an entrance is invisible and for a text effect is an empty line, noise or the `from` number. With scripting on, nothing changes in any browser.
